facts.statement: Patagosaurus lived during the Middle Toarcian period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Middle Toarcian~

facts.statement: Patagosaurus was first found in the Cañadón Asfalto Formation, dating to approximately 178 million years ago.
facts.quote: It was first found in deposits of the Cañadón Asfalto Formation, which date to around 178 million years ago.

facts.statement: Patagosaurus was first described by José Bonaparte in 1979.
facts.quote: The specimens were first described by José Bonaparte in 1979.

facts.statement: The specific name fariasi honors Ricardo Farias, whose land was the site of the initial discovery.
facts.quote: The specific name honours Ricardo Farias, on whose land the initial discovery was made.

facts.statement: Over twelve specimens have been referred to Patagosaurus, though some may belong to a different taxon.
facts.quote: Over twelve specimens have been referred to the species, although some of the material is probably from a unique taxon.

facts.statement: Advanced zircon dating indicates the fossils were deposited between 179 and 178 million years ago, corresponding to the Middle-Late Toarcian.
facts.quote: These layers have been recently re-dated, finding out thanks to advanced zircon datation that the bones of the three genera and all the vertebrates of Las Charcitas member where deposited in between 179 and 178 million years, that is Middle-Late Toarcian.

facts.statement: Patagosaurus possessed typical sauropod features including a long neck, small head, long tail, and quadrupedal stance.
facts.quote: Both ages exhibit the typical features of a sauropod: a long neck, small head, a long tail, and quadrupedal stance.

facts.statement: Juvenile Patagosaurus differed from adults in the mandible, pectoral girdle, pelvis, and hindlimb, though overall anatomy was similar.
facts.quote: The juvenile exhibits features different from the adult in regions like the mandible, pectoral girdle, pelvis, and hindlimb, although overall their anatomy is quite similar.

facts.statement: Patagosaurus is estimated to have been about 16.5 meters long and weighed approximately 7.88 metric tons.
facts.quote: It has been estimated that it was about 16.5 m long and weighed about 7.88 t.

facts.statement: An earlier 1997 estimate suggested Patagosaurus was approximately 15 meters long and weighed 9.44 metric tons.
facts.quote: An earlier estimate by John S. McIntosh and his colleagues in 1997, found that Patagosaurus was approximately 15 m long, and also 9.44 metric ton in weight, similar to the later estimates by Holtz.

facts.statement: Based on its broad, high, and short adult mandibles, Patagosaurus likely had a short, high, and broad snout, typical of most sauropods.
facts.quote: Based upon how broad, high and short the adult articulated mandibles of Patagosaurus are, its snout would have been short, high and broad as well, a typical feature of most sauropods.

facts.statement: Histological studies indicate Patagosaurus replaced its teeth every 58 days.
facts.quote: Based on histological studies, an individual of Patagosaurus would have replaced a tooth every 58 days, similar to 62 days for Camarasaurus, and 34 days for Diplodocus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether MACN CH 934 belongs to Patagosaurus, as its teeth differ significantly from those of other specimens attributed to the genus.
facts.quote: However, the teeth of MACN CH 934 are very different from those of both lower jaws (MACN CH 933 and MPEF-PV 1670), so it can be identified as another sauropod from the same deposit as Patagosaurus.

facts.statement: Patagosaurus shares similarities with related taxa like Cetiosaurus and Volkheimeria, primitive genera like Barapasaurus and Amygdalodon, and derived sauropods like Diplodocus and Camarasaurus.
facts.quote: The material of Patagosaurus is similar to closely related taxa like Cetiosaurus and Volkheimeria, more primitive genera such as Barapasaurus and Amygdalodon, and more derived sauropods like Diplodocus and Camarasaurus.

facts.statement: The sacral vertebrae of Patagosaurus measure a total length of 540 mm, while the entire sacrum measures 920 mm.
facts.quote: The sacral vertebrae have a total length of 540 mm, with the total sacral length being 920 mm.

facts.statement: Adult femora in Patagosaurus are proportionately straighter and more ovoid in cross-section compared to those of juveniles.
facts.quote: The adult femora are proportionately different from the juvenile, being mostly straighter and more ovoid in cross-section.

facts.statement: A 2021 study classified Patagosaurus as a member of the family Cetiosauridae.
facts.quote: A 2021 study found Patagosaurus to be a member of Cetiosauridae.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses from 2020, 2021, and 2024 confirmed a close evolutionary relationship between Patagosaurus, Bagualia, Nebulasaurus, and Spinophorosaurus.
facts.quote: Successive phylogenetic analyses from 2020, 2021, and 2024 have confirmed a close relationship between Bagualia, Nebulasaurus, Patagosaurus, and Spinophorosaurus.

facts.statement: Patagosaurus was discovered in the Jurassic Cañadón Asfalto Formation, which was recently re-dated to the Late Early Jurassic (Middle Toarcian) period.
facts.quote: Patagosaurus was uncovered in the Jurassic Cañadón Asfalto Formation, originally thought to be Middle or Late Jurassic, but found recently to be Late Early Jurassic (Middle Toarcian) in age.

facts.statement: Patagosaurus avoided direct competition with other sauropods by having distinct tooth morphology, indicating significant dietary niche partitioning.
facts.quote: Despite coexisting with multiple other sauropod taxa, Patagosaurus was able to avoid direct competition with them, as its tooth morphology differed substantially from coeval sauropod taxa, a feature indicative of significant dietary niche partitioning in its ecosystem.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the thinner enamel of Patagosaurus may be an adaptation for consuming more abrasive vegetation.
facts.quote: The thinner enamel of Patagosaurus may be related to its consumption of more abrasive vegetation.

facts.statement: Patagosaurus lived in a hypersaline and alkaline lake environment similar to modern Lake Magadi, near volcanic areas like the Chon Aike Province.
facts.quote: The Chacritas Member hosted and hypersaline and alkaline lake similar to modern Lake Magadi in Kenya, while nearby environments where developed in a similar way to modern Waimangu Volcanic Rift Valley of New Zealand, with nearby volcanic influence of the Chon Aike Province
